Why is it dangerous to leave the basement window open in winter?
The basement cools down, the ground below the basement floor freezes, and the floor heaves
Because snow falls in
Because the humidity rises
The ground below the basement floor is normally frost-free; but cold air can freeze it as well.
What happens beneath a cold store with poor insulation?
The zero isotherm penetrates deeper year by year, down to 6–12 m, and the floor and the building heave
The soil dries out and shrinks
Nothing, the soil absorbs the cold
The groundwater warms up
The frost moves downwards until the heat loss of the soil is made up by the heat flowing from the Earth’s interior.
What protects against frost beneath a cold store?
A thermal insulation layer and underfloor heating below the insulation
A thicker reinforced concrete floor on its own
Compacting the soil
Waterproofing
The insulation slows the heat loss and the underfloor heating keeps the ground above freezing – the two together are the safe solution.

On an infill plot in the city centre, sheet piles are being driven with a vibrator. The street wall of the neighbouring house, built around 1900, cracked within two weeks, and 2 cm of settlement was measured at the plinth. Beneath it there is saturated fine sand.
The vibration of the vibrator compacts the saturated, loose fine sand. Within the 20–30 m zone of influence of the source, vibration must be measured in the neighbouring building.
A corner of a warehouse built on sandy gravel on the bank of the Danube settled after the rapid passing of the spring flood wave. Tiny sand cones were visible at the toe of the slope.
During rapid drawdown the groundwater beneath the bank stays high, a strong flow starts towards the river, and this carries away the fine grains – the sand cones are the washed-out material.
A round, three-metre hole opened overnight in the yard of a house in Eger, and the back wall of the house tilted. An old wine cellar cut into tuff runs beneath the plot.
In the soaked tuff the vault of the cellar collapsed and the ground moved towards the cavity. A trough or a collapse appears at the surface.
The floor of the new cold store (−28 °C) began to bulge from the third year, the storage racks tilted and the doors jammed.
Below the floor the frost penetrates deeper year by year, and ice lenses grow in the silty layer. Thermal insulation and underfloor heating are needed.
At dawn, shaking woke the town’s residents. Several chimneys fell, and diagonal cracks appeared in the walls of old adobe houses.
Fallen chimneys, wall cracks: an intensity of at least VII. The effect of the earthquake decreases with distance from the focus, and soft ground amplifies it.

Diagonal cracks opened in the wall of a single-storey house with 0.6 m deep foundations at the end of a dry summer, and by winter they had almost closed. The house stands on high-plasticity clay, with large poplars growing in the garden.
Expansive clay: it shrinks when it dries and swells when it gets wet, and the cracks open and close with the seasons. In detail: Foundations on unfavourable ground ↗
The basement window was left open all winter. The basement floor heaved and cracked, and in spring it settled back.
Through the open window the cold froze the ground below the basement floor too. Frost heave is followed by settlement on thawing.
When an excavation was being dewatered, the water pumped from the sump was cloudy and sandy for days. The soil beneath the foundation of the neighbouring house loosened, and the house settled.
From quicksand the pump draws out the sand along with the water. Cloudy water is a warning sign: dewater with filtered wells or a filter layer.
The new metro tunnel passed beneath the building. In half a year the building settled by 5 cm, and the main walls and vaults cracked.
A tunnel is a cavity too: the ground moves inwards around the excavation, and a settlement trough travels along at the surface. Continuous building monitoring is needed in such cases.
Next to a high-performance machine in a printing works, the floor of the factory hall settled over time. As the machine spun up, the machine foundation vibrated conspicuously strongly at one speed.
A machine foundation is a dynamically loaded foundation. If the speed of the machine falls close to the natural frequency of the system, resonance occurs.
A farmstead on the Great Plain, with loose, saturated sand beneath the house. After an earthquake the house tilted, and sand bubbled up from cracks in the yard.
Liquefaction: cyclic shearing in loose, saturated sand raises the pore water pressure, and the soil loses its bearing capacity. The sand boil is its sign.

During rapid drawdown, when the groundwater stays higher than the river
During a slow, steady rise
